title: Near-Eligibility Allowance After a Hardship Denial — Non-Covered Discount, Hospital Account (Encounter Billing)
content:
The patient's most recent assistance determination under the Financial Assistance Program (Charity Care) decides the near-eligibility allowance on the non-covered discount percent of an insured Hospital Account (Encounter Billing) account.

**Which case counts.** Only a case in approved, denied, expired or revoked status is a determination; a submitted, pending-documents or withdrawn case is not, whatever date it carries. The most recent determination is the one with the latest determination date. Of determinations dated the same day, an approval, expiry or revocation counts as more recent than a denial, and of two denials the one recorded first counts.

**Clause.** The allowance applies when that most recent determination is a denial whose determination date falls no more than 365 days before the day the discount is posted: a case of the Riverbend Medical Hardship Assistance (above 400% FPL) tier denied as assets above limit adds 10 percentage points to the non-covered discount percent; a case of that tier denied as income above limit adds 5 percentage points; any other case, a most recent determination that is not a denial, an older determination or no determination adds none.

## Decision table

| Most recent determination | Tier | Denial reason | Determined within 365 days of posting | Points |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| denial | Riverbend Medical Hardship Assistance (above 400% FPL) | assets above limit | yes | 10 |
| denial | Riverbend Medical Hardship Assistance (above 400% FPL) | income above limit | yes | 5 |
| denial | any other tier, or another reason | any | either | none |
| denial | any | any | no | none |
| approval, expiry or revocation | any | any | either | none |

## Cases (hypothetical)

- A hardship denial for assets above limit dated exactly 365 days before the posting day adds 10 points; dated 366 days before, it adds none.
- A hardship denial and an approval of another case dated the same day: the approval counts as more recent, so none.
- A hardship denial followed by a later application still in submitted status: the submitted case is not a determination, so the denial remains the most recent determination.
